title: A radius of convergence you can't see
sub: The Taylor series of 1/(1 + x²) at 0, with more and more terms.

frames.caption: f(x) = 1/(1 + x²): smooth everywhere, no jumps, no corners. Its Taylor series at 0 is 1 − x² + x⁴ − x⁶ + …
Degree 2. Inside |x| < 1 (between the dashed lines) the polynomials close in on f; outside, they swing ever more wildly.
Degree 4. Inside |x| < 1 (between the dashed lines) the polynomials close in on f; outside, they swing ever more wildly.
Degree 8. Inside |x| < 1 (between the dashed lines) the polynomials close in on f; outside, they swing ever more wildly.
Degree 16. Inside |x| < 1 (between the dashed lines) the polynomials close in on f; outside, they swing ever more wildly.
Degree 32: perfect inside |x| < 1, hopeless outside it. Adding terms makes things worse out there. The radius of convergence is 1, even though f is smooth on the whole real line.
Why 1? Allow complex x: 1 + x² = 0 at x = ±i, where f blows up. Those points are at distance 1 from 0, and a power series can't reach past the nearest singularity, even one that's off the real line.
